title: “FOOLISHNESS.”
paragraphs: “FOOLISHNESS.”
That’s what they called it.

A bleeding Man nailed to wood.
Muscle torn. Back shredded. Crown of thorns pressed into sweating skin.
Arms stretched wide under a darkening sky.
And Paul said… that is power.
Let’s not sanitize it.
First Epistle to the Corinthians — Chapter 1

The church in Corinth loved brilliance.
Philosophy. Rhetoric. Status.
They wanted a Messiah who dazzled.
Instead, they got a crucified Carpenter.
“For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.” (1 Cor. 1:18)
Foolishness.

The Greek word carries the sting of absurdity. Moronic. Irrational.
A Savior who doesn’t conquer Rome — but bleeds under it.
Here’s the tension.

We want strength that flexes.
God chose strength that breaks.

We want crowns.
He chose thorns.

We want spectacle.
He chose shame.
And that shame… saved us.
The Scandal
Crucifixion wasn’t just execution. It was humiliation theater.

Skin split open.
Blood tracing ribs.
Breath scraping in and out of collapsing lungs.
A sign above His head mocking His kingship.

To Greeks, it was intellectual nonsense.
To Jews, it was a stumbling block (v.23).
Because Deuteronomy says, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.”
Cursed.
So how can the Messiah hang there?
Open loop.
Because the curse wasn’t His.
It was ours.
The Pivot
Here is the holy exchange.

Your lust.
Your pride.
Your secret addiction.
Your bitterness you rehearse at night.
Naïve? No.
Transferred.
Paul says Christ became for us wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption (v.30).
The cross offends logic because it dismantles ego.
You cannot boast at Golgotha.

Your résumé cannot climb that hill.
Your intellect cannot decode salvation.
Your morality cannot purchase it.
The cross levels kings and addicts alike.

It says:
“You bring sin. I bring blood.”
And that blood is enough.
The Power Hidden in Weakness
God chose what is weak to shame the strong (v.27).
Why?
So that no human being might boast in the presence of God.

The cross is not God losing.
It is God luring pride to its execution.

Satan thought it was victory.
Hell celebrated early.
Then Sunday happened.
The “foolish” cross became the doorway to resurrection.
Brother, Sister — Hear Me
If you feel disqualified…
If your past screams louder than your prayers…
If shame tells you, “You blew it too badly this time”…
Look again at the cross.

That “foolish” act is the wisdom that rescues you.
That “weak” Savior is the power that remakes you.

Some scholars interpret Paul’s contrast in 1 Corinthians 1 as both rhetorical and theological — confronting Greek philosophy while revealing a deeper spiritual blindness. But Paul’s point is crystal: salvation is not achieved by human brilliance. It is received by faith in Christ crucified.
Jesus didn’t die to impress you.
He died to redeem you.
So boast in nothing else.

Not your gifting.
Not your church role.
Not your clean record.
Boast in the Lord.
Because the cross offended logic —
—and saved the world.
Come to Him.

Repent.
Believe.
Lay your pride down at the wood that held your Savior.
